key.name: presentation-effects
key.summary: Presentation mode: chip and mark per trigger
key.description: Trigger id → (chip, mark). Ids: keys, click, drag, scroll, gesture. chip: shown in the panel; mark: rings at a click, a line from a drag's start to the pointer (keys, scroll and gesture have none). A drag is shown also with click chip and rings off; with both drag switches off it shows as a long press. Missing ids take the built-in default (all on).

key.name: key-detail
key.description: "activity": a symbol for every key; "classes": letter, digit, symbol, space and the names of non-printing keys (Return, Shift, …); "shortcuts": like classes, but with Ctrl, Alt or Super held the key itself (Ctrl + T); "characters": the typed character. rg-helper caps this at its max-detail (default "shortcuts", set by root in /etc/rg-helper.conf), because any process of the logged-in user can ask it for keys.

key.name: window-rules
key.description: WM class of the focused window → "global" (same as no rule), "off" (no effects at all), "mouse" (no keys; clicks, drags and the wheel still show), "activity", "classes", "shortcuts" or "characters" (key labels, capped by rg-helper's max-detail). Windows without a rule get key-detail. A rule may be more or less revealing than key-detail.

key.name: window-classes-request
key.summary: Ask for the open windows (written by prefs)
key.description: Not a user setting. Prefs changes it to have the extension write open-window-classes.

key.name: open-window-classes
key.description: Not a user setting. WM class, app name and icon of each open window, for prefs' "Show active window classes".

key.name: effect-mode
key.description: "ridiculous": playful effects where you type and click; "presentation": keys and shortcuts at a fixed place on screen, e.g. for screen recordings.

key.name: show-effects
key.description: Off: a pause in both modes, no effects, no sounds and no XP, e.g. during a call. Also in the top bar menu.

key.name: panel-indicator
key.description: A button in the top bar, in both modes: its menu pauses effects, switches sounds (ridiculous mode) and opens the settings. In ridiculous mode it can also show the level (ridiculous-xp-indicator).

key.name: presentation-target
key.description: "subtitle": one line at the bottom centre; "heading": one line at the top centre; "card": a card in a corner with rows for modifiers, key and scroll.

key.name: presentation-monitor
key.description: "primary": always the primary monitor; "pointer": the monitor with the mouse pointer.

key.name: presentation-idle-ms
key.summary: Pause before presentation mode fades out (ms)

key.name: presentation-style
key.summary: Look of the panel and its chips
key.description: dark, light, high-contrast (opaque, thick borders, for compressed video) or custom (presentation-custom-*).

key.name: presentation-custom-panel
key.description: As #rrggbb.

key.name: presentation-custom-opacity
key.summary: Custom style: panel opacity in percent

key.name: presentation-custom-text
key.description: As #rrggbb.

key.name: presentation-custom-chip
key.description: As #rrggbb; the chip's fill, its border is a darker shade.

key.name: presentation-accent
key.summary: Accent colour: the desktop's or presentation-accent-color
key.description: For click rings, drags and held keys. system follows the accent colour in GNOME Settings → Appearance (GNOME 47+, blue before).

key.name: presentation-accent-color
key.description: As #rrggbb; used when presentation-accent is custom.

key.name: ridiculous-effects
key.summary: Ridiculous mode: image, sound and shake per trigger
key.description: Trigger id → (image, sound, shake). Ids: typing, delete, return, combo, nav, click, drag, motion, scroll, swipe, pinch, touch, levelup. Missing ids take the built-in default. A trigger with all three off shows nothing; typing and Return still earn XP.

key.name: ridiculous-sounds
key.description: Off: no sounds at all, without changing the sound switch of each trigger in ridiculous-effects. Also in the top bar menu.

key.name: effect-preview-request
key.description: Not a user setting. "mode:trigger#n": the extension shows the trigger's effect (ids of ridiculous-effects or presentation-effects) as if it happened, with its switches, while that mode is on; n only makes each press a change.

key.name: ridiculous-char-labels
key.summary: Show the typed key on effects
key.description: Ridiculous mode: typed keys and shortcuts carry the key as a coloured label, at the focused window's key detail level.

key.name: ridiculous-xp-indicator
key.summary: Show the XP level in the top bar
key.description: Ridiculous mode: typing earns XP, deleting costs it; the level shows on the top bar button and the progress to the next one in its menu (needs panel-indicator). XP counts also when this is off.

key.name: ridiculous-xp-state
key.description: Not a user setting. Total XP, level, total XP at the start of the level, total XP for the next level. Reset it to start over at level 1.

key.name: animate-labels
key.description: Ridiculous mode: effects move (grow, turn, fly), windows shake, a level-up sets off fireworks. Presentation mode: chips fade in and out, click rings expand. When off, or with Reduce Animation on, nothing moves or shakes: effects stand still and fade out, a level-up shows a calm message. When the shell has animations disabled, effects are shown unanimated for the same time.

key.name: animation-status
key.summary: Shell animation status (written by the extension)
key.description: Not a user setting. Lets the prefs window show whether the shell allows animations: "available"; "reduced" (Reduce Animation is on); "inhibited" (the shell disabled them, e.g. software rendering or a remote session); "unknown" (extension not running).

key.name: warn-helper-missing
key.summary: Notify when rg-helper is not installed
key.description: Show a notification (once per session) when the helper is not installed and the extension runs in limited mode. Set to false by the notification's "Don't show again". A helper that is installed but not working is always reported.

key.name: helper-status
key.description: Not a user setting. Lets the prefs window show the helper's state without starting it: "subscribed"; "connecting" (waiting for the helper, or it is restarting); "missing" (not installed); "failed" with the reason; "unknown" (extension not running).

key.name: helper-notices-shown
key.summary: Helper notices already shown (written by the extension)
key.description: Not a user setting. The shell session the notices were shown in, and their kinds ("missing", "failed"), so a notice is shown at most once per session although the extension is disabled on every screen lock.
